name: שֶׁמֶר
summary: Shemer owned the hill that Omri king of Israel bought for two talents of silver, and Omri “called the name of the city that he built after the name of Shemer, the owner of the hill, Samaria (שֹׁמְרוֹן)” (1Ki 16:24): scripture itself derives the name of the northern capital from this man's. The same name is borne by a Levite of the sons of Merari, an ancestor of Ethan the singer (1Ch 6:31), and in the pausal form שָׁמֶר by the Asherite son of Heber (1Ch 7:34) who is called Shomer two verses earlier. Scripture does not explain the name. It is the plain noun of the root שמר, “keeping, watch”; the only common noun of that shape in scripture is the singular behind שְׁמָרִים “lees”, so “lees” (a name from the vineyard) cannot be ruled out.

evidence.note: “He bought the hill שֹׁמְרוֹן from שֶׁמֶר for two talents of silver, and built on the hill, and called the name of the city that he built after the name of שֶׁמֶר, the owner of the hill, שֹׁמְרוֹן.”
In the line of Ethan the Merarite: “son of Amzi, son of Bani, son of שָׁמֶר”.
“The sons of שָׁמֶר: Ahi and Rohgah, Hubbah and Aram”: the Asherite called שׁוֹמֵר in 7:32.
The city's later character, with the root's own verb: “the statutes of Omri are kept (וְיִשְׁתַּמֵּר)”.
The root's sense: “the keeper (שׁוֹמֵר) of Israel”.

note: 1Ch 6:31 is 6:46 in English numbering (TIPNR key Shemer@1Ch.6.46). Shomer@1Ch.7.32 is listed here as well as under names/shomer.json because 1Ch 7:34 spells him שָׁמֶר. BDB's v.ef.ab also counts 1Ch 8:12 שָׁמֶד (Shemed, a different name, TIPNR Shemed@1Ch.8.12). Samaria (שֹׁמְרוֹן, v.ef.ak) is a place and has no name entry; its form is the participle-like שֹׁמֵר with ‑ôn, so the city's name sounds like “watch-place” while being named for Shemer.
